• Likely recurring spend
• Observed price increases over time
• Unusual or material transactions worth reviewing

The scan runs locally in your browser. Your CSV is not uploaded to a server.

Software spend audits often start with a spreadsheet and a pile of card or bank statements.

Drop in a CSV, run the scan locally in your browser, and get a review list backed by the transaction data you supplied.

It is deliberately simple: transaction evidence first, human review after.

name: Orisift
tagline: One API to check phones, email domains, IPs and domains
description: Orisift is a developer API for checking contact and network data. Send a phone number, email address, IP address or domain to POST /v1/lookup. Phone checks cover format, numbering plan and reserved fiction ranges such as UK 020 7946 0xxx and US 555-0100 to 0199. Email checks look at the domain: MX, Null MX, DNS and a match against 8,986 throwaway-provider domains. IP checks flag special-purpose, bogon and reserved ranges and read reverse DNS. Domain checks read A, MX, NS, SPF and DMARC. Each response gives a verdict and its evidence. Orisift does not check mailboxes, carriers or phone liveness. Get 3 free checks a day without an account, or 500 credits on signup. Node/TS SDK: @orisift/sdk on npm.
bio: Building Orisift: one API that checks phones, email domains, IPs and domains.
story: Forms kept saving numbers from ranges reserved for fiction and emails on domains with no mail servers. Format checks passed them all.
verdict_reason: Live developer API product with documented endpoints, published npm SDK, real example responses, and a working signup/credit system. Product does what the submission describes.

name: SolveForge

SolveForge is browser-based practice for the online tests McKinsey, Bain and BCG use to screen candidates before interviews. For Bain, it has timed numerical, logical, verbal and situational judgement sections, plus full TestGorilla-style and SOVA-style mock tests. BCG guides are live and BCG practice is coming.

It's for people who just got a test invite and have about a week to prepare: MBA students, grads and consultants switching firms. Full prep packages elsewhere run $69 to $129, and a lot of free material still teaches a McKinsey game that was retired in 2025. SolveForge gives you a free scenario for each main game, free guides for every test, and one-time passes from $29 with no subscription. Every question is original, and we're upfront that these are practice recreations, not the real tests.
bio: At SCIMS we provide software solutions to help make users lives easier.
story: I sat the McKinsey Solve assessment myself. When the invite came, I went looking for practice and couldn't find anything good: most of it was out of date, overpriced, or didn't feel like the actual games under a real clock. So I built what I wished I'd had. It's rebuilt from what's publicly known about each game, it's honest about what's confirmed and what's just candidate-reported, and it's cheap enough that a stressed candidate can try it free before paying anything. Bain and BCG came next, because people who apply to one of these firms usually apply to all three.
verdict_reason: Live, real product offering practice simulations for consulting-firm assessments, with explicit non-affiliation disclaimer and no fabricated testimonials/metrics.

verdict_reason: Live, functional vocabulary platform with daily quests, multiplayer word games, spaced repetition, and progress tracking that match the submission's description.
